accepted.sentence: An inertial navigation system estimates position by measuring acceleration and rotation, since satellite signals cannot reach operating depth.
Operators often favor passive listening, locating distant activity from received sounds without transmitting detectable pulses.
Active sonar sends acoustic pulses and analyzes their echoes to estimate range, although transmissions can reveal the craft’s presence.
Before rising, the crew checks for traffic and uses available sensors to confirm a safe route toward the surface.
During an emergency ascent, compressed air can force water from ballast spaces, restoring positive buoyancy.
On diesel-electric models, engines run near the surface to recharge batteries, then stop before quieter travel at depth.
Trim tanks shift water between the bow and stern to keep the hull level as its load changes.
Acoustic decoys can imitate a vessel’s sound signature, drawing an incoming torpedo away from its intended target.
